# Aleph v0.1

Aleph is a programming language whose primary authors and readers are AI agents. Goals: few tokens, native speed, correctness on the first attempt, safe by default. Human readability is NOT a goal of the source text; humans read the generated explanation (`aleph explain`).

## 1. Source files
`.aph`; UTF-8; outside strings only printable ASCII and LF. LF only; no tabs, trailing spaces or empty lines; exactly one final LF. One file = one module (imports v0.2).

## 2. Lexical structure
One space between tokens. Column 0 = item; one leading space = `fn` body line. ident `[a-z][a-z0-9]*`; int `0|-?[1-9][0-9]*`; float `-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`; string `"..."` escapes `\n \t \" \\`; `@f` fnref; `.f` field; `x:` param; `[1 2]`; ops `+ - * / % == != < <= > >=`. Keywords: `fn type use let do ex doc if try some none ok err else has isok empty nil true false and or not neg match`.

## 3. Top-level items and canonical order
Order: `use` by full line text, `type` by name, `fn` by name (`main` last). Body: <=1 `doc`, then `ex E = E`+ (E001; unless `main`/effectful), then `let`/`do`*, then one result `E`. Items: `use CAP ["PREFIX"]`; `type NAME FIELD*` (field `f:T`; ctor `NAME a b`; access `.f e`); sum `type NAME | V FIELD* | ..` (ctor `V a`); `fn NAME PARAM* -> TYPE` (param `x:T`; `main` no params -> `unit` or `res unit str`). `fn`/`type`/variant names unique, not builtin/type names (P001).

## 4. Types
`i64 f64 bool str unit`; `list T`; `opt T`; `res T E`; `dict K V` (K i64/bool/str; expr `dict K V` = empty; immutable, keys ascending, not showable/comparable); record; sum. Prefix, fixed arity. Static bidirectional checking; signatures explicit, `let` inferred; no conversions/subtyping/overloading; builtins generic, user fns not. `json`: `json x` (x jsonable: unit bool i64 f64 str json, list json, dict str json; NaN -> null; depth >256 -> R005).

## 5. Expressions
No parentheses; arity from signatures/ctors/builtins. `+ - * / %` 2 same numeric (`%` i64); `== !=` 2 same primitive -> bool; `< <= > >=` 2 numeric -> bool; `and or` 2 bool short-circuit; `not` 1 bool; `neg` 1 numeric; `if c a b` 3 bool/same; `[e..]` n>=1 list T; `empty T`/`none T` 1 type; `.f e` 1 field; `some`/`ok`/`err` 1; `try e` 1 res T E -> T or early err (fn returns `res U E`); `else e d` 2 opt/res default T; `has e`/`isok e` 1 -> bool; `match e V b.. E ..`: an arm per variant of e's sum, in order, a binder per field, same type. `@f`: fn value, only as higher-order arg.

### 5.1 Builtins (v0.1)
`name signature`; effectful: `!` then capability, if any.
args ()->list str
at list T,i64->opt T
cat str,str->str
contains str,str->bool
count str->i64
del dict A B,A->dict A B
eprint str->unit !
filter (A->bool),list A->list A
float str->res f64 str
fold (B,A->B),B,list A->B
get dict A B,A->opt B
int str->res i64 str
jbool json->opt bool
jdict json->opt dict str json
jint json->opt i64
jlist json->opt list json
jnum json->opt f64
join list str,str->str
jparse str->res json str
json T->json (T jsonable)
jstr json->opt str
keys dict A B->list A
len list T->i64
lower str->str
map (A->B),list A->list B
print str->unit !
push list T,T->list T
put dict A B,A,B->dict A B
range i64,i64->list i64
read str->res str str ! fs.read
rev list T->list T
show T->str (T primitive, list of primitive or json)
size dict A B->i64
slice list T,i64,i64->list T
sort list T->list T (T primitive)
split str,str->list str
sum list i64->i64
trim str->str
upper str->str
vals dict A B->list B
write str,str->res unit str ! fs.write

## 8. Capabilities (ADR-0008)
Deny by default. `use fs.read "PREFIX"` / `use fs.write "PREFIX"`. `net.host`/`env`/`time`: no builtins yet. Relative/absolute POSIX prefixes, normalized (empty/`.` dropped), `..` never covered. Empty prefix, `..`, or a filesystem capability without a path -> C003. Literals checked statically (C001/C002); computed paths at run time (R003). stdout/stderr allowed. Traps (JSON stderr, exit 70): R001 overflow, R002 division by zero, R003 capability, R004 stack, R005 allocation.

## Semantics
T005: params/lets/binders may not reuse a param/local/fn/ctor/builtin name. `ex` sides see globals only; examples are hermetic (fs denied -> R003, no args, output dropped). `print`/`eprint` add one LF (stderr flushes stdout). `show`: i64 decimal; f64 Rust `{:?}` (`1.0`, `0.1`, `1e20`); list `[1 2]` (str elements quoted, `[]` empty); top-level str raw; json compact. `jparse` RFC 8259, err `json: REASON at byte N`; `jint` integers, `jnum` any number. `upper`/`lower` ASCII only. `at` negative/oob -> `none`; `slice` clamps to `[0 len]`; `range a b` half-open (`a>=b` empty, >10,000,000 elements -> R005); `sort` ascending; `count` bytes; `split s ""` -> Unicode chars (`split "" ""` -> `[]`); `int` `-?[0-9]+` in i64 (leading zeros) else `err "invalid int"`; `float` `-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` else `err "invalid float"`. `ok`/`err` need an expected `res` type else T010. recursion >10,000 calls or deep evaluation -> R004. `main` `err e` -> stderr, exit 1.

## 9. Diagnostics (ADR-0011)
JSON lines: required `code severity file line col msg`; optional `node expected found fix canonical`; lowercase msg; `fix` (replace/insert) only when certain. Prefixes: L lex, P parse, F format, T type, C cap, E example, R runtime, X tool. Codes: L001-L002 P001-P003 F001 T001-T008 T010 E001-E002 C001-C003 R001-R005 X001-X011.

## 10. Canonical form (ADR-0003)
AST is truth; text is its canonical printing. `aleph fmt` prints it; `aleph check` rejects different text (F001) with `canonical`. Invariant: `print(parse(t)) == t`; `parse(print(ast)) == ast`.

## 11. Command line (`aleph`)
`llms` prints this text; `check FILE [--json]`; `fmt FILE [-w]`; `test FILE [--json]`; `run FILE [ARGS..]`; `build FILE -o OUT`; `explain FILE [--json]`; `ast FILE`; `tokens FILE` (v0.2). Exit 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 70 trap.

## Examples
Canonical, check-clean programs (verbatim from `tests/aph/`):

```
fn demo -> unit
 ex sort [3 1 2] = [1 2 3]
 ex else at [10 20] 1 0 = 20
 ex at [10] 2 = none i64
 ex slice [1 2 3 4] 1 3 = [2 3]
 ex push [1 2] 3 = [1 2 3]
 ex rev [1 2 3] = [3 2 1]
 ex sum [1 2 3] = 6
 ex float "1.5" = ok 1.5
 ex else float "x" 0.0 = 0.0
 ex and true false = false
 ex or false true = true
 ex not false = true
 ex neg 5 = -5
 ex == 2 2 = true
 ex != 2 3 = true
 nil
fn main -> unit
 print show sort [3 1 2]
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print cat "a" "b"
 do print show count "abc"
 do print show split "a,b,c" ","
 do print join ["a" "b"] "-"
 do print trim "  hi  "
 do print upper "aBc"
 do print lower "aBc"
 do print show contains "abc" "b"
 nil
```

```
use fs.read "data"
use fs.write "out"
fn up text:str -> str
 ex up "aB c" = "AB C"
 upper text
fn main -> res unit str
 let text try read "data/in.txt"
 let saved try write "out/up.txt" up text
 ok nil
```

```
fn pick o:opt i64 -> i64
 ex pick some 5 = 5
 ex pick none i64 = 0
 else o 0
fn plus r:res i64 str -> res i64 str
 ex plus ok 41 = ok 42
 ex plus err "x" = err "x"
 let n try r
 ok + n 1
fn main -> res unit str
 do print show pick some 5
 do print show pick none i64
 do print show else ok 7 0
 do print show else err "x" 9
 do print show has some 1
 do print show isok plus ok 41
 do print show isok plus err "x"
 let n try plus ok 41
 do print show n
 ok nil
```

```
fn add a:i64 b:i64 -> i64
 ex add 2 3 = 5
 + a b
fn inc n:i64 -> i64
 ex inc 1 = 2
 + n 1
fn positive n:i64 -> bool
 ex positive 1 = true
 > n 0
fn main -> unit
 do print show map @inc [1 2 3]
 do print show filter @positive [-1 0 2]
 do print show fold @add 0 [1 2 3 4]
 nil
```

```
type point x:i64 y:i64
fn shift p:point d:i64 -> point
 ex shift point 1 2 10 = point 11 2
 point + .x p d .y p
fn main -> unit
 let p shift point 1 2 10
 do print show .x p
 do print show .y p
 nil
```

```
fn fib n:i64 -> i64
 ex fib 0 = 0
 ex fib 1 = 1
 ex fib 10 = 55
 if < n 2 n + fib - n 1 fib - n 2
fn main -> unit
 print show fib 30
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print "out1"
 do eprint "err1"
 do print "out2"
 do eprint "err2"
 nil
```

```
fn main -> unit
 print show len args
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print show [1 2 3]
 do print show [1.0 2.5]
 do print show ["a b" "c"]
 do print show empty i64
 do print show 1.0
 nil
```
instruction: Complete the Aleph function below so that it does what its doc line says. Write the whole file: the function exactly as given (header, doc and ex lines), any ex lines of your own, the body, and any helper functions you need (each with at least one ex line). Do not write main. Reply with only the code, in one code block marked aleph.

problems.name: HumanEval_13_greatest_common_divisor
problems.prompt:
fn greatestcommondivisor a:i64 b:i64 -> i64
 doc "Return a greatest common divisor of two integers a and b"
 ex greatestcommondivisor 3 5 = 1
 ex greatestcommondivisor 25 15 = 5

problems.name: HumanEval_23_strlen
problems.prompt:
fn strlen string:str -> i64
 doc "Return length of given string"
 ex strlen "" = 0
 ex strlen "abc" = 3

problems.name: HumanEval_30_get_positive
problems.prompt:
fn getpositive l:list i64 -> list i64
 doc "Return only positive numbers in the list."
 ex getpositive [-1 2 -4 5 6] = [2 5 6]
 ex getpositive [5 3 -5 2 -3 3 9 0 123 1 -10] = [5 3 2 3 9 123 1]

problems.name: HumanEval_34_unique
problems.prompt:
fn unique l:list i64 -> list i64
 doc "Return sorted unique elements in a list"
 ex unique [5 3 5 2 3 3 9 0 123] = [0 2 3 5 9 123]

problems.name: HumanEval_35_max_element
problems.prompt:
fn maxelement l:list i64 -> i64
 doc "Return maximum element in the list."
 ex maxelement [1 2 3] = 3
 ex maxelement [5 3 -5 2 -3 3 9 0 123 1 -10] = 123

problems.prompt:
fn digitsum s:str -> i64
 doc "Task\nWrite a function that takes a string as input and returns the sum of the upper characters only'\nASCII codes.\n\nExamples:"

 ex digitsum "abAB" = 131
 ex digitsum "abcCd" = 67

problems.name: HumanEval_150_x_or_y
problems.prompt:
fn xory n:i64 x:i64 y:i64 -> i64
 doc "A simple program which should return the value of x if n is\na prime number and should return the value of y otherwise.\n\nExamples:"
 ex xory 7 34 12 = 34
 ex xory 15 8 5 = 5

problems.name: HumanEval_159_eat
problems.prompt:
fn eat number:i64 need:i64 remaining:i64 -> list i64
 doc "You're a hungry rabbit, and you already have eaten a certain number of carrots,
but now you need to eat more carrots to complete the day's meals.
you should return an array of [ total number of eaten carrots after your meals,
                                the number of carrots left after your meals ]
if there are not enough remaining carrots, you will eat all remaining carrots, but will still be hungry.

Example:

Variables:
@number : integer
    the number of carrots that you have eaten.
@need : integer
    the number of carrots that you need to eat.
@remaining : integer
    the number of remaining carrots thet exist in stock

Constrain:
* 0 <= number <= 1000
* 0 <= need <= 1000
* 0 <= remaining <= 1000

Have fun :)"
 ex eat 5 6 10 = [11 4]
 ex eat 4 8 9 = [12 1]
 ex eat 1 10 10 = [11 0]
 ex eat 2 11 5 = [7 0]
